subject: Trading
title: A Brief History of Forex
description: A micro-lesson that makes A Brief History of Forex usable.

hook.text: Until 1971, the US dollar was backed by gold at $35 an ounce. Then Nixon pulled the plug and currencies floated.

buildup.text: The Bretton Woods system pegged all major currencies to the dollar, which was pegged to gold since 1944.

discovery.text: When gold backing ended, currencies began floating—their value set by supply, demand, and market forces.

twist.text: Free-floating currencies created the modern forex market—and an entirely new asset class for traders.

climax.text: A decision to abandon gold in 1971 accidentally created the largest financial market in human history.

punchline.text: Ending one system birthed a trillion-dollar market.

quiz.question: What happened when the Bretton Woods system collapsed?
options: Currencies began floating freely, creating the modern forex market
